children: By Rob Curran
U.S. stocks rose for the second straight session amid growing optimism about upcoming earnings reports from so-called artificial-intelligence hyperscalers.

The broad S&P 500 rose 45.83 points, or 0.60%, to 7722.60 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite gained 308.43 points, or 1.18%, to 26477.81. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 15.99 points, or 0.03%, to 52377.57.

Treasury yields rose as traders awaited the Federal Reserve's policy decision Wednesday. The central bank is widely expected to hold rates steady, but hotter-than-anticipated readings of inflation in recent weeks suggest an increase remains possible.

The yield on the policy-sensitive two-year Treasury rose 0.026 percentage point to 4.735%. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note added 0.004 percentage point to 4.992% and the yield on the 30-year bond rose 0.004 percentage point to 5.304%.
The U.S. dollar rose sharply in anticipation of a hawkish statement from the Fed.

"Hiking probabilities took a leg down when tech-sector credit seemed to be under pressure," said strategists at British brokerage Standard Chartered Global Research, in a note to clients. "But tech and AI have rebounded, so downside financial-market risks are now less pronounced."
The Standard Chartered strategists estimated there was a roughly one-in-four chance that the Fed would surprise markets with a rate hike on Wednesday.
Gold futures rose $36.50, or 0.9%, to $4058.80 a troy ounce.
Oil futures fell $1.86, or 1.8%, to $99.90 a barrel in New York, falling for the second straight session. Oil traders cited chatter of diplomatic activity from the Middle East and Ukraine.

Economic data was generally better than anticipated. New home sales fell a modest 0.6% in September. Durable goods orders, or orders for manufactured products designed to last three years or more like refrigerators and cars, rose 1.8% last month. The latest reading of consumer confidence from the Conference Board showed an improvement in mood in October.
In another good sign for economic activity, shares of UPS rallied, rising 5.9% to $106.09, after the package-delivery giant forecast 2026 earnings ahead of Wall Street estimates.
Economically sensitive cruise lines rose after a surprisingly strong earnings report and indications of positive booking trends from Royal Caribbean.
Among major tech companies reporting earnings in the coming days, Google parent Alphabet rose 0.8% to $316.83. Microsoft slipped 0.2% to $531.44. Amazon rose 1.6% to $253.10.
Dutch chip-equipment maker ASM International boosted its 2027 sales forecast, citing AI demand. American depositary receipts rose 7.9% to $846.20.
Chip maker Broadcom and AI model maker Anthropic finalized a $63 billion debt deal to finance AI infrastructure.
Corning shares fell 1.1% to $126.30. The maker of fiber-optic materials projected continued growth in demand from data centers, which drove a 58% jump in third-quarter net income.
Earnings in other sectors were mixed.

Boeing shares fell 11% to $168.18, its biggest percentage loss since the depths of the pandemic in 2020, after the aerospace giant posted another quarterly loss. Higher costs at its commercial-jet unit offset strong sales growth at its defense, space and security unit.
Shares of hospital chain HCA Healthcare fell 3.3% to $449.96 after it reported a lower profit in the third quarter as treatment of more uninsured patients offset revenue growth.
General Motors rose 5.5% to $80.54 after the Detroit auto giant said it was moving its stock listing to the Nasdaq from the NYSE.
